newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban dissident, freed from jail, travels to Spain.
newsitem.headline: Cuban dissident, freed from jail, travels to Spain.

text.p: A Cuban dissident travelled to Spain on Sunday after having been released from prison earlier this month, diplomatic sources said.

The sources said Robier Rodriguez Leyva, who was arrested in 1992 and sentenced to 10 years in prison for rebellion, was flying to Madrid on Sunday evening. His release was requested by the government of Spain.
There was no immediate word on the release from Cuban government authorities.
The sources said that political prisoners in Cuba are sometimes freed on condition they leave the country, adding that last year Cuba released five political prisoners in this way.

Rodriguez, 34, had been among a group of people who founded a small dissident group in the eastern city of Santiago de Cuba in 1991. The group was disbanded the following year and its members arrested. Rodriguez was among Cuban prisoners whose release the Spanish government requested.

Cuba last year released some 170 prisoners serving sentences for crimes against state security, some of them unconditionally and some of them because they had completed their sentences, the sources said.
However, 1,200 people were serving sentences for crimes against state security, they said. These include many viewed by foreign critics of Cuba's one-party system as political prisoners.
